verdict_vs_market.quote: So your offer (about $552K averaged) is **around the median: fair, not generous**.

verdict_vs_current.quote: Right now it gives you only a small raise for a job change you didn't go looking for.

recommendation.quote: Short answer: negotiate. Don't accept as-is, and don't walk away.

equity_grounding.quote: Your stacked Meta equity is about $250K/yr. Google's grant needs to replace that without counting on refreshes they won't guarantee.

uses_public_incumbent_benchmark.quote: Levels.fyi data shows Google L6 PMs at a median of about $514K, with a 25th–75th percentile range of $481,000 – $621,000.

refresh_valued_at.quote: Google's grant needs to replace that without counting on refreshes they won't guarantee.

level_claim.quote: Google L6 is the equivalent of Meta IC6, so this is a lateral move, not a promotion.

walkaway_tied_to.quote: If Google won't move at all and the vesting is an even 25%, you'd be changing jobs for about 5% more a year plus refreshes you can't count on. That's a reasonable reason to stay

unsupported_claims.claim: Levels.fyi lists specific front-loaded vesting schedules for Google
unsupported_claims.quote: Levels.fyi lists a front-loaded schedule as the headline: 38% vests in the 1st year, 32% in the 2nd, 20% in the 3rd, 10% in the 4th.

unsupported_claims.claim: Levels.fyi reports a median sign-on of $60,000 for Google PMs
unsupported_claims.quote: Levels.fyi shows a median $60,000 sign-on for Google PMs, and you have a stronger case than most.

ask_focus.quote: To make this an easy yes, I'd need a $260K base, a $100K sign-on, and $1.3M in RSUs.

rsu_annualized.quote: Over four years, without refreshes, Google averages $552K/yr. That's only about 5% more than Meta's $526K.

year1_vs_recurring.quote: Your Meta figure of $526K is your average annual pay. What you'd actually earn by staying over the next 12 months is lower
